task.description:
CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR hard gate (WF-02 Step 1b) on REQ-168's design (lib/letflow/design/req168-wasm-memory-isolation.md, test/specs/REQ-168.md). This is the single highest-stakes design in this pipeline: CODE-DESIGNER's live verification found a genuine, previously-undocumented hazard in wasmex -- at extreme (non-guest-reachable) magnitudes, Wasmex.Memory.read_binary/4 can either hang the calling process forever (length=2^63, uncaught native panic with no receive timeout) or SIGABRT the entire OS process (length=2^40, confirmed live exit code 134 'Aborted (core dumped)'). Do not rubber-stamp this given the stakes, but ALSO exercise real caution reproducing it yourself.

SAFETY INSTRUCTION, READ BEFORE RUNNING ANYTHING: if you reproduce section 1.4's findings yourself, run each probe as a SEPARATE, isolated `mix run` invocation (not inside this agent's own long-lived shell session state, and never inside an ExUnit test process) so that a SIGABRT/hang only kills that one subprocess, not your own working session. Set an explicit timeout (e.g. `timeout 20 mix run ...`) on the length=2^63 hang probe specifically, since the design itself found this call never returns on its own. Do not skip this section's verification entirely out of caution -- reproducing at least the length=2^40 SIGABRT (bisected already in the design to a known-abort value) is the single most important verification in this gate, since the whole design's safety argument rests on it being real; just do it defensively (separate timed subprocess) rather than not at all.
acceptance_criteria: Independently reproduce section 1.3's finding that wasmex's own NIF cleanly bounds-checks 'moderate' out-of-range offset/length pairs (up through 2^32-1) with a clean {:error, _} tuple, no crash -- this one is safe to run inline/live without special precaution.

Independently reproduce, with the explicit subprocess/timeout precaution above, at least the length=2^40 SIGABRT finding (section 1.4 Shape B) -- confirm the process really does abort with exit code 134, not just trust the design doc's transcript.

Confirm section 2's core safety argument is sound: that Elixir's arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic makes offset+length computation exact at any magnitude (no wraparound possible), and that rejecting on memory_size fetched fresh via Wasmex.Memory.size/2 before ever calling any Wasmex.Memory accessor is sufficient to prevent the dangerous magnitudes from ever reaching wasmex -- check this reasoning for gaps, not just internal consistency.

Confirm section 1.5's per-instance memory isolation claim is real by reproducing it yourself (two Wasmex.start_link/1 instances of identical bytes, write via one's memory handle, read via the other's).
Confirm section 1.6's finding that three of Wasmex.Memory's own @specs are incomplete (silently omit the {:error, _} return path) by reading deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex/memory.ex yourself.

Confirm the module-location decision (new Letflow.Engine.Wasm.MemoryGuard, no new Task.Supervisor) is justified -- check the reasoning in section 3 for why no Task.Supervisor wrapper is needed here (unlike REQ-166/167's instantiation-time wrapping) given the design's own claim that only pre-validated, in-range calls ever reach Wasmex.Memory from this module.

Confirm the moduledoc content (section 6) accurately cites req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md section 7.2 -- read that section yourself and verify the quote is accurate, not paraphrased into something stronger or weaker than the original.

Confirm test/specs/REQ-168.md and the design's section 5.4 safety instruction (never test read/4 or write/4 with a value >= ~2^40) are both present and would actually prevent TEST-DESIGNER from writing a test that could abort a future CI run.
Full traceability table covers every real REQ-168 acceptance criterion from docs/requirements.yaml.
Zero literal Elixir implementation code in the design doc.
CRITICAL: the handoff's top-level status field (line 9) must be exactly PENDING/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/FAILED/ESCALATED/CANCELLED when you finish -- run mix letflow.lint_handoffs before finishing.

result.summary: Independently reproduced every live-verification claim in lib/letflow/design/req168-wasm-memory-isolation.md except one, which is factually wrong. CONFIRMED (all real, all rerun on installed wasmex 0.15.1, PATH including .asdf/shims + .cargo/bin, WASMEX_BUILD=true): section 1.3's full 9-row 'moderate out-of-range' table, reproduced verbatim via scratch/validator_probe_1_3.exs -- every probe (offset-beyond-size x2, length-past-end, write-side x2, the offset=2^64-10/length=20 wraparound shape, and both offset/length=2^32-1 cases) returned a clean {:error, "out of bounds memory access"}, no crash, no hang. Section 1.4 Shape B's SIGABRT, reproduced via scratch/validator_probe_sigabrt.exs run as an isolated `timeout 30 mix run --no-start ...` subprocess per the handoff's safety instruction: real exit code 134, stderr 'memory allocation of 1099511627776 bytes failed', shell reported 'Aborted (core dumped)' -- exactly as design section 1.4 claims. Section 1.5's per-instance isolation, reproduced via scratch/validator_probe_isolation.exs: two independent Wasmex.start_link/1 instances of identical bytes, write via instance A's handle, instance B reads back 0 (not 99), instance A still reads 99. Section 1.6's three incomplete @specs, confirmed by reading deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex/memory.ex directly: get_byte/3 @spec is number() (line 129), read_binary/4 is binary() (line 231), write_binary/4 is :ok (line 190) -- none declares the {:error, _} path the design's own probes (and mine) show all three actually return out-of-bounds; set_byte/4's @spec (:ok | {:error, binary()}, line 154) is indeed already complete, matching the design's claim this one was already correct. Section 6's moduledoc quote checked verbatim against req165-wasmex-process-boundary.md section 7.2 (lines 487-505) -- exact match, not strengthened or weakened. Section 3's no-new-Task.Supervisor reasoning checked against req166 section 2.2 and req167's CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor precedent (both DO add a dedicated Task.Supervisor for their instantiation-time risk): the distinction holds -- REQ-166/167 wrap a call that can itself crash/hang (Wasmex.start_link/1), while MemoryGuard only ever forwards pre-validated (offset, length) pairs that section 1.3 already showed wasmex's own NIF handles cleanly; this is a reasoned exception to the precedent's underlying principle (wrap the risky call), not a silent departure from it. test/specs/REQ-168.md's own T2 case 3 and its file-level safety banner correctly restrict the 2^63-magnitude case to check_bounds/3 only, matching design section 5.4 exactly -- this would prevent TEST-DESIGNER from writing a test that could abort CI. Traceability table (design section 8) covers all 6 of docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-168 acceptance_criteria verbatim, 1:1. Grepped the whole design doc for `defmodule`/`end`/`def ` -- only one defmodule/end pair (lines 284/343) wrapping @type/@doc/@spec declarations only, zero function bodies. BLOCKER FOUND: section 1.1's transcript is factually wrong. It claims `Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory) #=> {:ok, 65536}`. I ran the identical call against the identical installed dependency (scratch/validator_probe_1_3.exs) and it returns the bare integer 65536, not a tagged tuple -- `{:ok, size} = Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory)` raises a MatchError. This matches size/2's own @spec in deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex/memory.ex:78 (`pos_integer()`, not a tuple type) and matches how the design's own section 2 step 2 actually uses the value (`memory_size = Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory)`, a bare assignment, not a tuple destructure) -- so the design's actual algorithm is unaffected by this error, but section 1.1 itself, which this document explicitly stakes its credibility on ('Everything below section 1 is reproducible', 'every other section's safety claim rests on section 1's findings, not on wasmex's published docs'), is not accurately reproducible as written. This is exactly the class of error section 1.6 itself warns against (trusting a claimed return shape instead of the one actually observed), occurring one section earlier in the same document. Not blocking because it changes any @spec or test case, but blocking because a live-verification section presenting a false claim as confirmed fact is disqualifying in the single highest-stakes design in this pipeline -- a future reader (ELIXIR-DEV writing a doctest, or a later auditor) has no way to tell this one line apart from the rest of section 1's otherwise-accurate transcripts without re-deriving it, which is exactly what this gate exists to do once so no one else has to.

issues.description: Design section 1.1 (line 57) claims `Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory) #=> {:ok, 65536}`. Independently reproduced against the same installed wasmex 0.15.1 dependency: the call returns the bare integer 65536, not a {:ok, _} tuple (confirmed by both live execution and deps/wasmex/lib/wasmex/memory.ex:78's own @spec, `pos_integer()`). Fix the transcript to show the real return value (`Wasmex.Memory.size(store, memory) #=> 65536`) and re-check the rest of section 1's transcripts line-by-line against a fresh live run before resubmitting, since this is the one place this rework should not need a second pass to catch.
